tells: Formulaic launch-video opener using a punchy contrast pivot and 'Meet [Product]': "Site blockers ban YouTube. But YouTube is where half of us actually learn. Meet Goal Goose." (s1).
Rhetorical question answered immediately for faux-conversational punch: "A linear algebra lecture on YouTube? The goose is happy." (s3).
Overly smooth parallel rhythm with two back-to-back ', and' compound sentences: "Drift to a cat video, and the goose notices. Hydrogen writes what it says, and the warnings escalate." (s4).

Repeated symmetrical clause pairing across segments: "works out what on-track looks like, and where to send you back to" (s2) and "check that it's really a distraction, and that you won't lose your work" (s5).
Dramatic one-word sentence fragment for manufactured pacing: "Approved." (s6).
Slogan-like tagline built on a 'not X, but Y' antithesis plus generic startup phrasing ('focus buddy'): "A focus buddy that understands what you're doing, not just where you are." (s7).
Canned demo outro pairing a standalone product-name fragment with a clipped closing credit: "Goal Goose." followed by "Built today with Gemini 4." (s7).

segments.text: Site blockers just ban YouTube, which sucks since half of us learn there. This is Goal Goose.
First, you give the goose your goal. Gemini 4 Neon reads it once so it knows what counts as on track and where to send you back.
Every page, Gemini Decision 1 checks a screenshot against your goal in a split second. So on this linear algebra lecture on YouTube, the goose is totally happy.
If I wander to a cat video, the goose notices. Hydrogen writes the warnings, pushing harder each time.
Before eating anything, the goose's manager has to okay it. Decision 1 and Neon check it's really a distraction and make sure you won't lose your work.
Manager approves, so the goose eats the video and sends you back to the lecture you were watching.
Anyway, that's Goal Goose. Built it today with Gemini 4 so it understands what you're doing, whatever site you're on.
